claim: L1TD1 is a domesticated transposon protein derived from LINE-1 (L1) ORF1p.
source: The domesticated transposon protein L1TD1, derived from LINE-1 (L1) ORF1p, is an RNA-binding protein that is expressed only in some cancers and early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: L1TD1 is expressed only in some cancers and early embryogenesis.
source: The domesticated transposon protein L1TD1, derived from LINE-1 (L1) ORF1p, is an RNA-binding protein that is expressed only in some cancers and early embryogenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: L1TD1 is essential for maintaining pluripotency in human embryonic stem cells.
source: In human embryonic stem cells, it is found to be essential for maintaining pluripotency.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Emani et al., 2015; Närvä et al., 2012).

claim: L1TD1 expression is highly correlative with malignancy progression in cancer.
source: In cancer, L1TD1 expression is highly correlative with malignancy progression and as such considered a potential prognostic factor for tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: DNA hypomethylation induces the expression of L1TD1 in HAP1 human tumor cells.
source: Our findings reveal that DNA hypomethylation induces the expression of L1TD1 in HAP1 human tumor cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: L1TD1 depletion significantly modulates both the proteome and transcriptome.
source: L1TD1 depletion significantly modulates both the proteome and transcriptome and thereby reduces cell viability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: L1TD1 depletion reduces cell viability.
source: L1TD1 depletion significantly modulates both the proteome and transcriptome and thereby reduces cell viability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: L1TD1 associates with L1 transcripts.
source: Notably, L1TD1 associates with L1 transcripts and interacts with L1 ORF1p protein, thereby facilitating L1 retrotransposition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by RIP-seq data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: L1TD1 interacts with L1 ORF1p protein.
source: Notably, L1TD1 associates with L1 transcripts and interacts with L1 ORF1p protein, thereby facilitating L1 retrotransposition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: L1TD1 facilitates L1 retrotransposition.
source: Notably, L1TD1 associates with L1 transcripts and interacts with L1 ORF1p protein, thereby facilitating L1 retrotransposition.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by retrotransposition assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: L1TD1 is the only domesticated protein-coding gene that originated from LINE-1.
source: One example of such domesticated gene is LINE-1-type transposase containing domain 1 (L1TD1), which is the only domesticated protein-coding gene that originated from LINE-1 (long interspersed element 1 [L1]) (McLaughlin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to McLaughlin et al., 2014.

claim: L1TD1 shares sequence resemblance with L1 ORF1p.
source: L1TD1 shares sequence resemblance with L1 ORF1p, a nucleic acid chaperone protein with binding capacity to both RNA and DNA (Martin, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Martin, 2006.

claim: L1 ORF1p is a nucleic acid chaperone protein with binding capacity to both RNA and DNA.
source: L1TD1 shares sequence resemblance with L1 ORF1p, a nucleic acid chaperone protein with binding capacity to both RNA and DNA (Martin, 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Martin, 2006.

claim: L1 ORF1p contributes to the formation of L1 ribonucleoproteins (L1-RNPs).
source: L1 ORF1p contributes to the formation of L1 ribonucleoproteins (L1-RNPs), key factors for retrotransposition of L1 elements, but its co-factors are yet to be elucidated (Wallace et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Wallace et al., 2008.

claim: L1-RNPs are key factors for retrotransposition of L1 elements.
source: L1 ORF1p contributes to the formation of L1 ribonucleoproteins (L1-RNPs), key factors for retrotransposition of L1 elements, but its co-factors are yet to be elucidated (Wallace et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Wallace et al., 2008.

claim: L1TD1 is expressed predominantly only in early embryogenesis and germ cells.
source: L1TD1, also named embryonic stem cell-associated transcript 11 (ECAT11), is expressed predominantly only in early embryogenesis and germ cells and gets rapidly downregulated upon the exit from pluripotency (Iwabuchi et al., 2011; Mitsui et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Iwabuchi et al., 2011 and Mitsui et al., 2003.

claim: L1TD1 gets rapidly downregulated upon the exit from pluripotency.
source: L1TD1, also named embryonic stem cell-associated transcript 11 (ECAT11), is expressed predominantly only in early embryogenesis and germ cells and gets rapidly downregulated upon the exit from pluripotency (Iwabuchi et al., 2011; Mitsui et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Iwabuchi et al., 2011 and Mitsui et al., 2003.

claim: L1TD1 is dispensable for mouse development.
source: Although it is dispensable for mouse development (Iwabuchi et al., 2011), L1TD1 is essential for the maintenance of human pluripotency (Emani et al., 2015; Närvä et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Iwabuchi et al., 2011.

claim: L1TD1 regulates translation of a distinct set of mRNAs in human embryonic stem cells.
source: In the context of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), L1TD1 regulates translation of a distinct set of mRNAs (Jin et al., 2024), including core pluripotency factors (Emani et al., 2015), and was recently shown to facilitate the dissolution of stress granules (Jin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Jin et al., 2024 and Emani et al., 2015.

claim: L1TD1 facilitates the dissolution of stress granules in human embryonic stem cells.
source: In the context of human embryonic stem cells (hESCs), L1TD1 regulates translation of a distinct set of mRNAs (Jin et al., 2024), including core pluripotency factors (Emani et al., 2015), and was recently shown to facilitate the dissolution of stress granules (Jin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Jin et al., 2024.

claim: The L1TD1 gene was under positive selection during mammalian evolution due to its function in the maintenance of pluripotency in some species.
source: It has been proposed that during mammalian evolution the L1TD1 gene was under positive selection due to the function in the maintenance of pluripotency in some species (McLaughlin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to McLaughlin et al., 2014.

claim: L1TD1 is expressed in certain tumors, including germ cell tumors and colorectal cancers.
source: Apart from early development, L1TD1 is expressed in certain tumors, including germ cell tumors and colorectal cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by subsequent citations.

claim: L1TD1 was identified as a possible prognostic marker for medulloblastoma.
source: In this context, L1TD1 was identified as a possible prognostic marker for medulloblastoma (Santos et al., 2015) and colorectal tumors (Chakroborty et al., 2019), where its expression is highly correlative with malignancy progression (Urh et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Santos et al., 2015.

claim: L1TD1 was identified as a possible prognostic marker for colorectal tumors.
source: In this context, L1TD1 was identified as a possible prognostic marker for medulloblastoma (Santos et al., 2015) and colorectal tumors (Chakroborty et al., 2019), where its expression is highly correlative with malignancy progression (Urh et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Chakroborty et al., 2019.

claim: DNMT inhibitor treatment of non-small cell lung carcinoma patient-derived cells resulted in reduced cell viability and up-regulation of L1TD1.
source: DNMT inhibitor treatment of non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) patient-derived cells resulted in reduced cell viability and up-regulation of L1TD1, indicating an epigenetic control of the L1TD1 gene (Altenberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Altenberger et al., 2017.

claim: Xenograft tumors with NSCLCs overexpressing L1TD1 showed decreased tumor growth.
source: In addition, xenograft tumors with NSCLCs overexpressing L1TD1 showed decreased tumor growth, suggesting a negative impact of L1TD1 expression on tumor viability.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on previous research.

claim: L1TD1 was shown to be required for cell viability in medulloblastoma.
source: In contrast, L1TD1 was shown to be required for cell viability in medulloblastoma (Santos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Santos et al., 2015.

claim: Conditional deletion of DNMT1 in the murine epidermis results in the upregulation of mobile elements such as intracisternal A-particles (IAPs) and induced expression of L1TD1.
source: We have previously discovered that conditional deletion of the maintenance DNA methyltransferase DNMT1 in the murine epidermis results not only in the upregulation of mobile elements, such as intracisternal A-particles (IAPs) but also in the induced expression of L1TD1 (Beck et al., 2021, Table S1).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Beck et al., 2021.

claim: Inhibition of DNMT activity by aza-deoxycytidine in human NSCLCs results in the upregulation of L1TD1.
source: These findings are in accordance with the observation that inhibition of DNMT activity by aza-deoxycytidine in human NSCLCs results in the upregulation of L1TD1 (Altenberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Altenberger et al., 2017.

claim: Transcriptome analysis revealed the deregulation of 2385 genes in DNMT1 KO HAP1 cells compared to wildtype.
source: Transcriptome analysis revealed the deregulation of 2385 genes (log2FC >2, adjusted p-value<0.05) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The majority of deregulated genes in DNMT1 KO HAP1 cells were upregulated.
source: The majority of deregulated genes were upregulated and included, in addition to L1TD1, genes with function in transcription and cell differentiation and genes encoding melanoma antigen gene (MAGE) proteins and KRAB domain containing proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Expression of DNMT3A and DNMT3B was significantly upregulated in the absence of DNMT1.
source: In addition to these two gene classes, expression of the de novo methyltransferases DNMT3A and DNMT3B was significantly upregulated in the absence of DNMT1, suggesting a potential compensatory mechanism (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: DNA methylation at the L1TD1 promoter is significantly reduced in DNMT1 KO HAP1 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 1A, DNA methylation-specific PCR (MethyLight) analysis revealed significantly reduced DNA methylation at the L1TD1 promoter in DNMT1 KO cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: DNA hypomethylation at the L1TD1 gene correlated with a strong induction of L1TD1 mRNA and protein expression in DNMT1 KO cells.
source: DNA hypomethylation at the L1TD1 gene correlated with a strong induction of L1TD1 mRNA and protein expression in DNMT1 KO cells (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1B-D.

claim: In the absence of DNMT1, the methylation of L1 transposons was reduced and expression of L1 ORF1p was induced.
source: Similarly, in the absence of DNMT1 the methylation of L1 transposons was reduced and expression of L1 ORF1p, the ancestor of L1TD1, was induced (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: L1TD1 was preferentially localized in the cytosol of HAP1 DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells.
source: In accordance with previously published data with hESCs (Närvä et al., 2012), indirect immunofluorescence analysis revealed that L1TD1 was preferentially localized in the cytosol of HAP1 DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: L1TD1 showed a granular localization in HAP1 DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells.
source: We detected a similar granular localization of L1TD1 in HAP1 DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion showed significantly reduced cell proliferation.
source: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion are viable but showed significantly reduced cell proliferation and increased apoptosis (cleaved caspase 3) and DNA damage (γ-H2AX) (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion showed increased apoptosis.
source: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion are viable but showed significantly reduced cell proliferation and increased apoptosis (cleaved caspase 3) and DNA damage (γ-H2AX) (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion showed increased DNA damage.
source: HAP1 cells with DNMT1 depletion are viable but showed significantly reduced cell proliferation and increased apoptosis (cleaved caspase 3) and DNA damage (γ-H2AX) (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: Additional deletion of L1TD1 enhanced the antiproliferative effects of DNMT1 ablation.
source: Additional deletion of L1TD1 enhanced the antiproliferative effects of DNMT1 ablation.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: L1TD1 expression is regulated by DNA methylation.
source: These results suggest that L1TD1 expression is regulated by DNA methylation and its depletion affects cell viability in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: L1TD1 depletion affects cell viability in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
source: These results suggest that L1TD1 expression is regulated by DNA methylation and its depletion affects cell viability in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: 597 transcripts were enriched in L1TD1-RNPs compared to the input.
source: We identified 597 transcripts enriched (log2FC >2, adjusted p-value <0.05) in L1TD1-RNPs compared to the input (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 228 transcripts were identified as L1TD1-associated RNAs.
source: Only transcripts enriched (log2FC >2, adjusted p-value <0.05) in both assays (DNMT1 KO versus input and DNMT1 KO versus DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO) were considered as L1TD1-associated RNAs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 2), resulting in the identification of 228 transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: L1TD1 mRNA was detected as one of the top transcripts in L1TD1-RNPs.
source: Importantly, L1TD1 mRNA was detected as one of the top transcripts in L1TD1-RNPs (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The transcript of YY2 was enriched in L1TD1-RNPs.
source: Of note, the transcript of YY2, a retrotransposon-derived paralogue of yin yang 1 (YY1) (Tahmasebi et al., 2016), was also enriched in L1TD1-RNPs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by RIP-seq data.

claim: Transcripts of L1TD1, YY2, and ARMC1 were specifically enriched in L1TD1-RNPs obtained from DNMT1 KO cells compared to DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells.
source: Transcripts of L1TD1, YY2, and ARMC1 (as one of the RIP top hits) were specifically enriched in L1TD1-RNPs obtained from DNMT1 KO cells compared to DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells, whereas the negative control GAPDH did not show such enrichment (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by RIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: L1TD1-associated transcripts include enriched groups in cell division and cell cycle regulation.
source: Gene Ontology analyses of the 228 common hits indicated enriched groups in cell division and cell cycle regulation and, in accordance with a recent study (Jin et al., 2024), enriched transcripts encoding zinc finger and in particular KRAB domain proteins that have been implicated in the restriction of endogenous retroviruses (Rosspopoff and Trono, 2023; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: L1TD1-associated transcripts include enriched transcripts encoding zinc finger and KRAB domain proteins.
source: Gene Ontology analyses of the 228 common hits indicated enriched groups in cell division and cell cycle regulation and, in accordance with a recent study (Jin et al., 2024), enriched transcripts encoding zinc finger and in particular KRAB domain proteins that have been implicated in the restriction of endogenous retroviruses (Rosspopoff and Trono, 2023; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: L1TD1 associates with L1 transcripts.
source: Analysis of RIP-Seq using TEtranscript designed for the analysis of transposon-derived sequences (Jin et al., 2015), in the differentially expressed sets indicated an association of L1TD1 with L1 transcripts (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 3), which was also validated by qRT-PCR analysis of L1TD1 RIP samples (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEtranscript analysis shown in Figure 2D and qRT-PCR validation shown in Figure 2E.

claim: ERV and AluY elements were identified as L1TD1-RNP-associated transcripts.
source: In addition, we also identified ERV and AluY elements as L1TD1-RNP-associated transcripts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: 98 proteins were upregulated in DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells versus DNMT1 KO cells.
source: A comparison of the proteomes revealed 98 upregulated and 131 downregulated proteins in DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells versus DNMT1 KO cells (log2FC ≥1, adj. p-value≤0.05) (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 131 proteins were downregulated in DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells versus DNMT1 KO cells.
source: A comparison of the proteomes revealed 98 upregulated and 131 downregulated proteins in DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells versus DNMT1 KO cells (log2FC ≥1, adj. p-value≤0.05) (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A comparison of differentially expressed proteins with transcripts associated with L1TD1 identified only L1TD1.
source: A comparison of differentially expressed proteins with transcripts associated with L1TD1 identified only L1TD1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Modulation of the abundance of proteins encoded by L1TD1-associated transcripts is not the main function of L1TD1.
source: The lack of overlap between RIP-seq and proteomics data (except L1TD1) suggested that modulation of the abundance of proteins encoded by L1TD1-associated transcripts is not the main function of L1TD1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on the comparison of RIP-seq and proteomics data.

claim: L1 ORF1p was upregulated in the absence of L1TD1.
source: Interestingly, we discovered that L1 ORF1p was upregulated in the absence of L1TD1 (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Western blot analysis confirmed the increased expression of L1 ORF1p in HAP1 DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells compared to DNMT1 KO cells.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed the increased expression of L1 ORF1p in HAP1 DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells compared to DNMT1 KO cells (Figure 3C), while L1 transcript levels showed no significant change (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: L1 transcript levels showed no significant change in DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells compared to DNMT1 KO cells.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed the increased expression of L1 ORF1p in HAP1 DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells compared to DNMT1 KO cells (Figure 3C), while L1 transcript levels showed no significant change (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: L1TD1 attenuates the expression of L1 ORF1p.
source: This indicates that L1TD1 attenuates the expression of L1 ORF1p, suggesting a potential regulatory crosstalk between L1TD1 with its ancestor protein.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is inferred from the observation that L1 ORF1p is upregulated in the absence of L1TD1.

claim: Upon loss of L1TD1, 323 transcripts were upregulated and 321 transcripts were downregulated.
source: Upon loss of L1TD1, we identified 323 upregulated and 321 downregulated transcripts, respectively (log2-fold change ≥1; adjusted p-value<0.05) (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: About 25% of the differentially expressed proteins identified in the proteome analysis were also significantly deregulated at the RNA level.
source: About 25% of the differentially expressed proteins (34% of upregulated and 22% of downregulated proteins) identified in the proteome analysis were also significantly deregulated at the RNA level (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on comparison of proteomics and RNA-seq data.

claim: None of the deregulated transcripts, except L1TD1, was detected in L1TD1-RNPs.
source: However, none of the deregulated transcripts, except L1TD1, was detected in L1TD1-RNPs (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 2 and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on comparison of RNA-seq and RIP-seq data.

claim: The cellular function of L1TD1 might be independent of a deregulation of its associated mRNAs.
source: This finding was corroborated by qRT-PCR analysis of L1TD1-RNP-associated transcripts (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), suggesting that the cellular function of L1TD1 might be independent of a deregulation of its associated mRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on qRT-PCR validation shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Loss of L1TD1 resulted in upregulation of specific SINEs such as AluY elements.
source: Loss of L1TD1 resulted in upregulation of specific SINEs such as AluY elements (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEtranscript analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: L1TD1 affects the abundance of transposon transcripts in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that L1TD1 affects the abundance of transposon transcripts in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on TEtranscript analysis.

claim: L1TD1 was co-precipitated with L1 ORF1p from DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells.
source: Indeed, L1TD1 was co-precipitated with L1 ORF1p from DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: L1TD1 associates with L1 ORF1p in an RNA-independent manner.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B, L1TD1 associates with L1 ORF1p in an RNA-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by RNase treatment experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: Indirect immunofluorescence experiments revealed a partial co-localization of L1TD1 and L1 ORF1p in DNMT1 KO cells and OV-90 cells.
source: In agreement with their association in protein complexes, indirect immunofluorescence experiments revealed a partial co-localization of L1TD1 and L1 ORF1p in both cell lines (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: An average of 506 retrotransposition events were observed in DNMT1 KO cells in three independent experiments.
source: An average of 506 retrotransposition events were observed in DNMT1 KO cells in three independent experiments whereas DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells yielded over fivefold fewer colonies when transfected with the retrotransposition-competent reporter construct (86 retrotransposition events on average) (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by retrotransposition assay data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells yielded over fivefold fewer colonies when transfected with the retrotransposition-competent reporter construct (86 retrotransposition events on average).
source: An average of 506 retrotransposition events were observed in DNMT1 KO cells in three independent experiments whereas DNMT1/L1TD1 DKO cells yielded over fivefold fewer colonies when transfected with the retrotransposition-competent reporter construct (86 retrotransposition events on average) (Figure 4C and D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by retrotransposition assay data shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: L1TD1 enhances L1 retrotransposition in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells.
source: Combined, these data suggest that L1TD1 enhances L1 retrotransposition in DNMT1-deficient HAP1 cells and this effect is mediated through the association with L1 ORF1p and L1 RNA.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and is based on retrotransposition assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The domesticated transposon protein L1TD1 promotes L1 retrotransposition.
source: In this study, we show that the domesticated transposon protein L1TD1 promotes L1 retrotransposition.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on the retrotransposition assay results.

claim: L1TD1 deletion resulted in reduced L1 retrotransposition despite upregulation of L1 ORF1p.
source: L1TD1 deletion resulted in reduced L1 retrotransposition despite upregulation of L1 ORF1p, indicating that the higher levels of the transposon protein cannot fully compensate the loss of L1TD1.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on the retrotransposition assay and Western blot data.

claim: A positive effect of L1TD1 on retrotransposition was recently also observed upon L1TD1 overexpression in HeLa cells.
source: Interestingly, a similar effect has been previously described for the nonsense-mediated decay factor UPF1 (Taylor et al., 2013). UPF1 knockdown increased the amount of L1 mRNA and proteins but simultaneously reduced the effectiveness of the retrotransposition. A positive effect of L1TD1 on retrotransposition was recently also observed upon L1TD1 overexpression in HeLa cells (Jin et al., 2024).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Jin et al., 2024.

claim: The L1TD1 protein shares with its ancestor L1 ORF1p the non-canonical RNA recognition motif and the coiled-coil motif required for the trimerization.
source: The L1TD1 protein shares with its ancestor L1 ORF1p the non-canonical RNA recognition motif and the coiled-coil motif required for the trimerization but has two copies instead of one copy of the C-terminal domain (CTD), a structure with RNA-binding and chaperone function (Januszyk et al., 2007; Martin, 2006; McLaughlin et al., 2014; Naufer et al., 2019; Santos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with citations to multiple studies.

claim: L1TD1 has two copies instead of one copy of the C-terminal domain (CTD).
source: The L1TD1 protein shares with its ancestor L1 ORF1p the non-canonical RNA recognition motif and the coiled-coil motif required for the trimerization but has two copies instead of one copy of the C-terminal domain (CTD), a structure with RNA-binding and chaperone function (Januszyk et al., 2007; Martin, 2006; McLaughlin et al., 2014; Naufer et al., 2019; Santos et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with citations to multiple studies.

claim: L1TD1 not only binds to L1 transcripts but also associates with L1 ORF1p in an RNA-independent manner.
source: We show here that L1TD1 not only binds to L1 transcripts but also associates with L1 ORF1p in an RNA-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on RIP-seq and co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The presence of an additional CTD within the L1TD1 protein might enhance the RNA-binding and chaperone function of L1TD1/ORF1p heteromultimers.
source: We hence speculate that the presence of an additional CTD within the L1TD1 protein might thereby enhance the RNA-binding and chaperone function of L1TD1/ORF1p heteromultimers.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on speculation about the structural features of L1TD1.

claim: The majority of L1TD1-associated transcripts in HAP1 cells (69%) were also reported as L1TD1 targets in hESCs.
source: Interestingly, the majority of L1TD1-associated transcripts in HAP1 cells (69%) identified in our study were also reported as L1TD1 targets in hESCs, suggesting a conserved binding affinity of this domesticated transposon protein across different cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on comparison with a previous study (Jin et al., 2024).

claim: L1TD1 localizes to high-density RNP condensates and enhances the translation of a subset of mRNAs enriched in the condensates.
source: The same study (Jin et al., 2024) showed that L1TD1 localizes to high-density RNP condensates and enhances the translation of a subset of mRNAs enriched in the condensates.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to Jin et al., 2024.

claim: L1TD1 ablation leads to a significantly changed proteome.
source: Our mass spectrometry data showed that L1TD1 ablation leads to a significantly changed proteome.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section and is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: None of the proteins encoded by the mRNAs associated with L1TD1 showed significantly changed steady state levels in the absence of L1TD1.
